title: The Argentina Square
logline: Mickey Aldrin builds a board game out of eleven years of Lily's Sunday phone calls, where every friend's special power is their worst habit. Marshall wants to invest, Lily's sabotage turns it into a hit, and Ted, Robin and Barney's playtest becomes a five-hour feud over a game none of them bothered to read the rules of.
coldOpen: Kids, your Aunt Lily's dad invented forty-one board games. Forty of them were disasters. The forty-first was much worse. It worked.

couch.line: Nobody, Luke. It took us five hours to figure out why.

guests.name: Roz
guests.role: owner of Roz's Grocery and Games on Amsterdam since 1979; gravel-voiced, unimpressed by everything, and only stocks games that end friendships

guests.name: Wes
guests.role: an eager customer convinced the game is secretly about his own friend group, in which he is the Marshall and a man named Doug is the Ted

scenes.summary: Mickey pitches Back to the Booth: five friends, one booth, every special power is a worst habit, all sourced from Lily's Sunday calls. Flashback proves he was rolling dice the whole time. Marshall wants to invest; Lily vows the game never touches a shelf. Mickey needs a focus group with no lives, and Ted, Robin and Barney walk in.

beats.line: Marshall, whatever my dad is selling tonight, we are not buying.
Lilypad, he said this one's different.
He said that about Raccoon Party.
Raccoon Party was ahead of its time.
It came with a raccoon, Marshall.
Only the deluxe edition.
Forty failed games, kids, and I finally figured out what they were missing.
Players?
People I know. Meet Back to the Booth. Five best friends, one booth, and every piece gets a special power.
Like Bigfoot's power to avoid every camera ever invented?
Here's the twist. Every special power is that friend's worst habit.
Dad. You made a game about my friends?
Marshall Eriksen. The Investor. Once per game, Marshall must give all his money to a man in plaid.
You're wearing plaid.
Sweetheart, that's a coincidence.
Lily, it's like he looked right into my soul.
He looked right into our checking account.
Where did you even get all this?
From you! Eleven years of Sunday phone calls.
I told you things because you never listened. I could hear dice, Dad.
I was listening!
Kids, every Sunday call with Mickey went about the same way.
Uh-huh. Robin hid in a coat closet so she wouldn't have to say I love you. Uh-huh.
Mister Aldrin. You've been rolling my display dice for an hour.
Uh-huh. Ted corrected a priest. At a funeral. Uh-huh.
Yahtzee!
Sorry, sweetie. Go on. The priest.
Dad, I called to tell you Marshall proposed, and you yelled Yahtzee.
In my defense, it was a Yahtzee.
And Roz's Grocery and Games wants to see it tomorrow.
The place that took the raccoon?
He's assistant manager now.
Lily. I want to invest.
No.
I haven't even said how much!
Marshall, it's on your card.
What's Lily's special power?
Hers isn't finished yet.
Don't bother. That game is never touching a shelf.
Fine. First I need a focus group. Three people with strong opinions and no lives.
Hey, guys! What are we doing tonight?

scenes.summary: Mickey pitches Roz, who only stocks games that end friendships. Lily's attempt to talk her out of it sells her on it. Lily secretly buys all twenty copies for a bonfire, turns away a man named Wes whose friend Doug is another Ted, and Roz orders five hundred more. Mickey calls Lily his first customer; Marshall discovers she used the investment account.

beats.line: The next morning, Mickey pitched the only store in Manhattan that still let him in.
Mickey Aldrin. Fifteen years of rolling my display dice, and you never bought a single die.
Today, Roz, I'm selling. Back to the Booth.
I have one rule for my shelf. If it ends a friendship, it goes by the register.
Monopoly ended my marriage. Bestseller, twenty-two years running.
Roz, as the game's lead investor—
He's not an investor.
Emotional investor.
Roz, I'll be honest. This game would really hurt people.
Hurt how?
Ted's piece makes everyone lose a turn while he explains where words come from.
Go on.
Robin's piece flees to Argentina if anyone says feelings.
Keep going.
Grown adults would be screaming at each other for hours!
I'll take twenty.
Sweetheart! Thirty years, and you finally closed a deal for me!
Marshall, let's go call the printer. Lily, I'll call you Sunday!
You never call on Sunday.
This Sunday I'm calling.
Roz. I'll take all twenty.
All twenty?
They're gifts. For a bonfire.
Hi! Do you have Back to the Booth? The one with the five friends?
Sold out.
No! It's about my exact friend group. I'm the Marshall.
Our Ted is this guy Doug. Corrects waiters. Owns cowboy boots for no reason.
Red ones?
Red ones.
Oh no. There's two of them.
I'll pay triple. Doug needs to see this.
Doug needs help. Go home and hug your Doug.
Twenty copies gone in nine minutes. A grown man begging at my register.
I'm ordering five hundred.
Did somebody say five hundred?
Your daughter bought every copy.
My first customer.
Big fan.
Lilypad, where'd you get the money for twenty games?
The investment account.
You invested!

scenes.summary: Marshall runs the playtest like a deposition. Ted, Robin and Barney read their special powers and are outraged at how accurate they are; flashback to Ted's birthday fire. Five hours later the game is a real feud: Ted feelings Robin to Argentina, Barney and Robin trade fake articles, and nobody has reached the booth once. Barney threw out the rulebook. Robin storms off to Argentina; Marshall doubles the order.

beats.line: That night, Marshall ran Mickey's focus group like a deposition.
For the record, please read your special powers aloud. Mister Mosby, you're the boot.
The Lecture. Once per turn, Ted may explain where a word comes from. Everyone else loses a turn.
That's slander. Which, interestingly, comes from the Old French—
And we've all lost a turn.
Robin. Flight Risk. If anyone says the word feelings, Robin's piece moves to Argentina.
There's no Argentina on the board.
It's on the box lid. Mickey ran out of board.
Barney. The Bro Code. Barney may invent any rule, as long as it has an article number.
Lies. Article twelve: Barney's card is a lie.
You just did it.
Article thirteen: no I didn't.
These are cartoons. Mickey has met us four times, and once he called me Tim.
Ted, the candles melted at your birthday while you explained the word wish.
That never happened.
Make a wish, Ted!
Actually, wish comes from the Old English. Which is fascinating, because—
Ted. The candles.
It shares a root with an ancient word for desire, so really—
Ted, the tablecloth!
So every wish is a tiny prayer.
Ted, there's a fireman here who'd like you to explain the word evacuate.
The fire department called it a small fire.
Dad. You set your own birthday on fire with a vocabulary lesson.
The important thing, Penny, is that everybody learned a word.
Let the record show the game begins at eight-oh-two.
Let the record show it is now one-fifteen in the morning.
Two more spaces and I'm in the booth.
Robin. How are you feeling about that?
Don't.
Feelings.
Argentina. Again.
Article forty: Argentina is now a permanent address.
Article forty-one: Barney's piece goes down the garbage disposal.
You can't write articles! You're not a bro!
Article forty-two: I'm a bro.
This is exactly what you do. Somebody gets close and you're on a plane.
And you gave a lecture on the word wish while a building burned.
A tablecloth burned! A building is a structure!
Guys! This is supposed to be a fun game about how terrible we all are.
Says the guy who invented forty-two rules tonight.
Forty-three. Article forty-three: Ted just lost a turn.
Five hours and nobody can stop playing. Greatest focus group in history.
Wait. Five hours. Has anyone actually reached the booth?
No one. Not once.
Did anybody read the rulebook?
I threw it out. Bros don't read rulebooks.
Article?
One.
Fine. Tomorrow, Mickey's launch at Roz's. New box, new rulebook, and we settle this.
Fine.
Great. I have a lot of feelings about it.
That's it. I'm going to Argentina.
Mickey? Double the order. The focus group hates each other.

scenes.summary: Launch day. Lily guards the display and her anti-sales pitch sells three copies at a time. Mickey knows she bought the twenty to burn, because he remembers what she told him about Scooter in 1994. The feuding trio arrives for a rulebook: the one rule is that nobody wins alone. Mickey explains every Sunday story ended with four friends rescuing the fifth. Lily's card is Second Chance; she uses it on her dad. Robin flees to Argentina and comes right back. Marshall uses his power: the envelope is empty.

beats.line: Sir, put down that box. That game destroys friendships.
Perfect. It's for Doug.
You've been here since six. Every time you say destroys friendships, I sell three.
Lily. You came to my launch.
I came to stop your launch.
I know. You bought those twenty copies to burn them.
How did you know that?
You did the same thing to Scooter's mixtapes in 1994. You told me on a Sunday.
You remember that?
Roz! One copy of Back to the Booth. We need the rulebook.
You're the boot.
I'm... yes.
Lose a turn.
Lily, five hours and nobody won. Your father's game is broken.
The focus group would like a rulebook. Ours was thrown out under Article one.
Read them the rules, kiddo. There's only one.
Nobody wins alone. The game ends when every piece is back in the booth.
It's a cooperative game.
We spent five hours trying to beat each other at a game you can only win together?
That's the most Canadian thing I've ever heard.
Thank you.
Dad. Why would you make it like that?
Because every story you ever told me went the same way. One of you did something dumb.
And the other four went and got them. Eleven years of Sundays, kiddo. That was every story.
You were listening.
I was listening. I was also rolling dice. I'm not a saint.
What's my special power? I never looked.
Inside the lid.
Second chance. Once per game, bring any piece back to the booth. Even one who doesn't deserve it.
beats.title: Lily Aldrin: Second Chance
lines: Once per game, bring any piece back to the booth.
Even one who doesn't deserve it.

beats.line: That's your worst habit, kiddo. I should know. I've used it about forty times.
Dad. I'm using my special power.
On who?
Who do you think?
Okay. That's a lot of feelings. I'm going to Argentina.
Give her a minute. She always comes back. That's the rule.
Argentina was closed.
Mickey. I would like to use my special power.
Marshall—
Lilypad. It's on my card.
Once per game.
Marshall, this envelope is empty.
Yeah. Lily spent it all on your first twenty copies.
Kids, I said Mickey's game worked. I didn't say it sold. Four hundred copies, three hundred and eighty of them to your Aunt Lily.
And every Sunday, Mickey called first. He yelled Yahtzee just once more, when Marvin was born. In his defense, it was a Yahtzee.
